name: The Free Salters' Ledger
description: A ledger bound in sailcloth and crusted white at the edges, kept by the Salt-King in a careful clerk's hand: every sack carried out of the Saltmound's heart for six years, four stone to a barge, and beside each the name of whoever carried it, Gullhithe boatmen and Sedgehithe widows' sons, and what they were paid in salt.

name: The Undersong's Clapper
description: The tongue of the Drowned Quarter's great bell, bronze the length of your arm, green with forty fathom of the Mere and bright where Corwen Lisle's hands held it. It hums against your back when you walk, very faintly, on a note you cannot quite name.

name: The Merry Tally's Name-Board
description: A lake-boat's name-board, prised off her bow and kept in the Salters' camp for the brass screws: THE MERRY TALLY in white letters on blue, and under it, scratched small with a knife-point, W.M.

name: Weighmaster's Drop
description: A little brass drop-weight on a cord, stamped with the Charter's scales and the mark of the Charter Scale: one ounce, true. Prudence Gauge gives one to anybody who brings her beam level, which is not many people.

name: Drowned Seal-Ring
description: A heavy brass ring black with the Mere, a Tallyman's seal cut into its bezel: a pair of scales and the letters J.H. Brought up off the bottom by one of Corbin Vell's cormorants and dropped by the perches with the other things a bird cannot eat. Alderman Hale lost one like it in the Cold, twelve years ago.

name: Mere Pike
description: A middle cut of lake pike, the head and tail kept by whoever caught it. Eaten roasted on a stick on the shingle it is the best thing on the Mere; eaten in the city it has been tolled twice.

name: Unsealed Salt
description: A twist of grey-white Salt Isles salt with no Charter seal on the sack it came from. It tastes exactly like the taxed kind, which is the whole trouble.

name: The Salters' Pay-Board
description: A slate from the Free Salters' camp in the Saltmound, ruled into a pay-roll of marks and sacks.

name: The Salt-King's Compliments
description: A letter the Salt-King never sent, folded small and sealed with a thumbprint of salt.

name: The Patience's Dive-Log
description: A salvor's waxed dive-log, its last pages in Corwen Lisle's hand.

name: A Drowned Quarter Street-Plate
description: A plate of black Builders' stone prised off a corner of the Drowned Quarter, cut with signs, and the salvors' chalked reading of them on the back.

name: Seed Pearl
description: A grey pearl no bigger than a lentil from a Wold Water mussel. The Row's tithe-clerks will not bother to tithe them; a jeweller in Tollmere will buy a hatful.

name: Mere Pearl
description: A freshwater pearl the size of a pea, pink-grey with a light that moves in it, from the great mussels of the Wold Water's mouth. One shell in two hundred.
